promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: The effects of exercise on body systems

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a function of the skeleton?
questions.explain: The skeleton stores minerals such as calcium, not oxygen; it also supports, protects and makes blood cells.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of a ball and socket joint?
questions.explain: The hip and shoulder are ball and socket joints, allowing a wide range of movement in all directions.

questions.q: What is the role of a tendon?
options: To cushion the ends of bones
questions.explain: Tendons attach muscle to bone, whereas ligaments attach bone to bone.

questions.q: During flexion at the elbow the biceps acts as the agonist. Which muscle acts as the antagonist?
questions.explain: In this antagonistic pair the triceps relaxes as the biceps contracts to flex the elbow.

questions.q: A netball player raises her arm sideways, away from the midline of her body, to intercept a pass. Which movement is this?
questions.explain: Abduction is the movement of a limb away from the midline of the body.

questions.q: Where in the lungs does gaseous exchange take place?
questions.explain: The alveoli provide a large, moist surface area for the exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide.

questions.q: What happens to the diaphragm during inhalation (breathing in)?
questions.explain: The diaphragm contracts and flattens to increase the volume of the chest cavity, drawing air into the lungs.

questions.q: Which equation correctly shows how cardiac output is calculated?
options: Cardiac output = stroke volume x heart rate
Cardiac output = heart rate ÷ stroke volume
Cardiac output = stroke volume + heart rate
Cardiac output = heart rate - stroke volume
questions.explain: Cardiac output is the volume of blood pumped per minute, found by multiplying stroke volume by heart rate.

questions.q: Why do veins contain valves?
options: To speed up blood flow to the lungs
To prevent the backflow of blood
To withstand very high blood pressure
questions.explain: Veins carry blood at low pressure, so valves stop the blood flowing backwards.

questions.q: An athlete has a stroke volume of 70 ml and a heart rate of 80 beats per minute. What is her cardiac output?
questions.explain: Cardiac output = stroke volume x heart rate, so 70 x 80 = 5600 ml per minute.

questions.q: What is the by-product of anaerobic exercise?
questions.explain: Anaerobic respiration breaks down glucose without oxygen, producing lactic acid.

questions.q: Which word equation correctly represents aerobic respiration?
options: Glucose + oxygen → energy + carbon dioxide + water
questions.explain: Aerobic respiration uses oxygen to release energy, producing carbon dioxide and water as waste.

questions.q: Which of these activities relies predominantly on the aerobic energy system?
questions.explain: Long-duration, lower-intensity activities such as a marathon are fuelled mainly by the aerobic system.

questions.q: Why can anaerobic exercise only be maintained for a short period of time?
options: Because too much oxygen is delivered to the muscles
Because lactic acid builds up and causes muscle fatigue
Because carbon dioxide levels fall too low
questions.explain: Lactic acid accumulates during anaerobic work, causing fatigue that limits the effort to short bursts.

questions.q: A sprinter runs the 100 metres in under 11 seconds at maximum effort. Which energy system is she mainly using?
questions.explain: Short, high-intensity efforts rely on the anaerobic system because oxygen cannot be supplied quickly enough.

questions.q: Which of the following is a short-term (immediate) effect of exercise?
questions.explain: Heart rate rises immediately during exercise, whereas the other options are long-term adaptations.

questions.q: Cardiac hypertrophy is a long-term effect of training. What does it mean?
options: The heart muscle becomes larger and stronger
The heart beats faster at rest
The number of red blood cells decreases
questions.explain: Regular aerobic training enlarges and strengthens the heart muscle wall.

questions.q: A trained endurance athlete has a lower resting heart rate than an untrained person. What is this adaptation called?
questions.explain: Bradycardia is a resting heart rate below 60 beats per minute, a long-term effect of aerobic training.

questions.q: How does increased capillarisation benefit a trained performer?
options: It decreases the amount of oxygen reaching the muscles
It improves gaseous exchange and oxygen delivery to the muscles
It reduces the size of the heart
questions.explain: More capillaries improve the delivery of oxygen and nutrients and the removal of waste at the working muscles.

questions.q: After several months of weight training a performer notices their muscles have become visibly larger. Which long-term adaptation explains this?
questions.explain: Sustained resistance training increases the size of muscle fibres, known as muscle hypertrophy.
